producer_report.summary:
I added `docs/spec.toml`, covering Olympus sections 1 to 6 as sourced requirements, and `xtask/tests/spec.rs`, which checks it against BRIEF.md. One policy test fails in this snapshot, only because the new test file is untracked.

Each quote must be a verbatim substring (whitespace collapsed) of the body under its stated heading. Because of that, a real quote paired with the wrong heading, or with its parent heading, fails.

The other negative cases cover a duplicate id, a dangling supersedes target, a requirement with no source, and an unknown kind or status. A coverage test checks R1 to R8 and sections 1 to 5, and open-question sides are checked like sources. I found no real conflict in sections 1 to 6, so the spec has no open questions.

I also added decision D114 to `docs/decisions.md`, enforcement row M33 to `docs/enforcement.md`, and a line to `CHANGELOG.md`.

The spec tests (16), the other xtask unit tests, clippy with warnings denied and `cargo fmt --check` all pass. A case-insensitive search of the five touched files found none of the banned words or fragments.

`every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists` in `xtask/tests/policy.rs` fails here. `policy.rs` lists files with `git ls-files`, and `spec.rs` is untracked, so it reports the nine test names in the M33 row as missing. They exist in `spec.rs`. I could not stage the file to confirm the test passes once it is committed.

checks_run.note: Unit tests and spec pass. policy::every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists fails only in this snapshot because policy.rs reads `git ls-files` and spec.rs is untracked. It lists the nine spec test names as missing. It should pass once Athena commits the files. I cannot stage files here.

checks_run.command: Grep for banned words and fragments over the five touched files

criteria_check.criterion: docs/spec.toml has, for each requirement, an id, a plain cohesive statement, a kind (goal, requirement, constraint or acceptance), a status (active or superseded), and one or more sources, each a verbatim quote plus its BRIEF.md heading. It covers Olympus sections 1 to 6 and has at least one requirement for each of R1 to R8 and for sections 1 to 5.
criteria_check.evidence: the_real_spec_passes and the_real_spec_covers_r1_to_r8_and_sections_1_to_5 pass. an_unknown_kind_or_status_does_not_parse passes, so kinds and statuses outside the allowed sets are rejected.

criteria_check.criterion: Duplicates across the brief are merged into one requirement with several sources. Any conflict or open choice in Sri's words is recorded as an open question quoting both sides, with no resolution.
criteria_check.evidence: Merged requirements carry several [[requirement.source]] entries in docs/spec.toml. I found no real conflict in sections 1 to 6, so there are no [[open_question]] entries. D114 and the spec header both say open questions are never resolved. open_question_sides_are_checked_like_sources passes.

criteria_check.criterion: docs/decisions.md records the spec format and the choice of TOML, with alternatives. It notes that sections 7 to 10, the governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda follow in a second job.
criteria_check.evidence: D114 is at docs/decisions.md line 2681. It names the format, TOML and the alternatives, and says sections 7 to 10, the governing philosophy and the addenda follow in a second job.

criteria_check.criterion: No statement in the spec or the new test says who runs Athena or where, so xtask/tests/policy.rs still passes. No governance files change.
criteria_check.evidence: A case-insensitive search of all five touched files for the banned words and fragments found no matches. athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where passes. Only CHANGELOG.md, docs/decisions.md, docs/enforcement.md, docs/spec.toml and xtask/tests/spec.rs changed. The run of `cargo test -p xtask` has one policy failure, every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists, because spec.rs is untracked (see open_issues).

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask --test spec`. It passes on the real spec. Each in-memory negative case makes the checker fail: a quote that is not a verbatim substring of BRIEF.md after whitespace collapse, a duplicate id, a supersedes target that does not exist, and a requirement with no source. A further test fails if any of R1 to R8 or sections 1 to 5 has no requirement.
criteria_check.evidence: All 16 tests pass, including a_quote_that_is_not_in_the_brief_fails, a_duplicate_id_fails, a_dangling_supersedes_fails, a_requirement_without_a_source_fails and a_missing_requirement_for_a_section_or_r_fails.

criteria_check.criterion: The checker also confirms each quote sits under its stated heading, not just somewhere in BRIEF.md. A negative case pairs a real quote with the wrong heading and fails. Run `cargo test -p xtask`.
criteria_check.evidence: a_real_quote_under_the_wrong_heading_fails and a_subsection_quote_under_its_parent_heading_fails pass. The rest of `cargo test -p xtask` passes (33 unit tests, 8 of 9 policy tests). The ninth, every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists, fails only because the file is untracked.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean. `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` still passes.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` are clean. In `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`, 8 of 9 pass. The ninth, every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists, fails only because xtask/tests/spec.rs is untracked in this snapshot and policy.rs lists only tracked files. The nine test names in the M33 row exist in spec.rs.

open_issues: policy::every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists fails in this snapshot because xtask/tests/spec.rs is untracked. It should pass once the candidate is committed. I could not confirm that here.
xtask/Cargo.toml is unchanged, because toml and serde were already dev-dependencies. It is a listed deliverable, so this departs from the brief.
The known failing athena-data digest test is untouched.
learnings: policy.rs finds the files to scan with `git ls-files`, so a new untracked test file is invisible to M24 until it is committed.
The Hermes row in BRIEF.md holds a banned word, so the spec quotes a fragment before it.
desires: A way to stage new files so policy.rs's git ls-files sees them.
